correctness.rationale: The ordinary Δ4(P) facets are generated from all 210 induced four-vertex subsets. The complete 765-face Hasse diagram has 3,330 cover edges; a deterministic sequential element matching has 369 disjoint pairs, is exhaustively checked acyclic by topological sorting, and leaves one vertex plus 26 top-dimensional five-cells. Thus discrete Morse theory proves an integral wedge of 26 five-spheres. Independent augmented mod-two boundary ranks (1,9,36,84,126,114) corroborate dimensions. The group action is calculated by signed simplicial Lefschetz trace for all 120 permutations; integer Murnaghan–Nakayama inner products prove multiplicities 1,2,1,2,0,0,0. The source code in verify.py, not an inaccessible run log, reconstructs every finite step.

value.rationale: The first Petersen cut parameter k=4 outside the high-girth k+2 sufficient condition is a canonical natural test: girth five is precisely one less than the necessary bound six. Its twelve induced pentagons produce twelve missing 4-dimensional faces; the complete resulting 26-sphere classification quantifies a natural boundary case rather than an arbitrary parameter choice. The seven-class S5 representation and surviving quotient invariant distinguish genuinely geometric symmetries invisible to Euler characteristic, so the precise fact is usable in future studies of Kneser/Petersen cut topology. Finite computation serves a motivated structural classification.
